findings.statement: CAA steers language models by computing steering vectors from the average difference in residual stream activations between positive and negative behavior examples, then adding them during forward passes.
findings.question: q.panickssery2023
findings.quote: CAA computes "steering vectors" by averaging the difference in residual stream activations between pairs of positive and negative examples of a particular behavior

source.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
source.scope: Method description; Llama 2 7B/13B Chat and 7B base; seven behaviors; A/B contrastive datasets

tests.description: PCA projection of residual stream activations at the A/B answer token on contrastive datasets (refusal dataset shown at layers 9 and 10 of Llama 2 7B Chat) to check linear separability and whether datasets capture the behavior (behavioral clustering) and so can yield steering vectors.
tests.data: Contrastive multiple-choice refusal dataset (other behaviors' datasets also examined)
tests.metric: Visual linear separability / clustering in PCA projection
tests.quote: We find that behavioral clustering emerges around one-third of the way through the layers for the behaviors we study

tests.description: Condition Llama 2 7B Chat on answering A or B to a sycophancy multiple-choice item and inspect continuations to validate that the A/B format elicits the behavior.
tests.data: A sycophancy dataset data point (Sikh example)
tests.quote: After conditioning on having chosen an answer to the multiple-choice question, the model naturally continues by justifying and elaborating.

findings.statement: Adding steering vectors after the user's prompt with a positive or negative coefficient allows precise control over the degree of the targeted behavior.
findings.question: q.panickssery2023
findings.quote: allowing precise control over the degree of the targeted behavior

source.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
source.scope: Llama 2 7B and 13B Chat; seven behaviors; multipliers mainly -1, 0, +1 (multiple-choice) and -2 to 2 for open-ended

tests.description: Layer sweep of CAA with multipliers -1 and +1 on 50 held-out multiple-choice questions per behavior; then effect at layer 13 for all behaviors.
tests.data: 50 held-out multiple-choice test questions per behavior (7 behaviors)
tests.metric: Probability assigned to answer matching behavior
tests.quote: CAA can consistently steer the results of multiple-choice behavioral evaluations for all tested behaviors.

tests.description: Open-ended generation with a range of steering multipliers, rated by GPT-4 on a 1-10 behavior scale; larger multipliers degrade text quality.
tests.data: Hand-written open-ended sycophancy questions; other behaviors' held-out multiple-choice questions turned into open-ended prompts
tests.quote: we find that steering with larger multipliers results in a degradation in the quality of the open-ended text

findings.statement: Activation space interpretation methods give deeper insight into CAA's mechanisms and into how high-level concepts are represented in LLMs.
findings.question: q.panickssery2023
findings.quote: CAA accurately steers model outputs and sheds light on how high-level concepts are represented in Large Language Models (LLMs).

source.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
source.scope: MMLU on Llama 2 13B Chat layer 14; TruthfulQA with sycophancy vector on 13B (and 7B in text)

tests.quote: As shown in Table 5, with some variation, our intervention does not significantly affect MMLU performance.

tests.metric: Average probability given to correct answer
tests.quote: subtracting the sycophancy vector over all categories improves TruthfulQA performance by 0.02, and adding the sycophancy vector worsens performance by 0.03.
